t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style. A limestone header band with a small eyebrow and a large light-weight sans-serif headline in sentence case. Below, a strict grid of square-cornered tiles butted edge to edge in alternating deep navy and warm limestone: one oversized lead tile, the rest equal. Each tile carries a huge light numeral with a slash, an uppercase step title and short text for <CONTENT>. One limestone tile holds a framed navy hairline isometric drawing of a pipe joint with dimension lines and mono tags. Flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: Steps set as a navy and limestone Swiss tile grid with giant slash numerals, one tile carrying a dimensioned joint drawing like a figure in a poster.
strengths: giant light slash numerals make the sequence instantly readable
navy/limestone tiles, light headline and square corners match the brand
drawing tile gives the steps a concrete subject
maps cleanly to a token-only CSS grid
body text is short and readable
weaknesses: the joint drawing is incoherent: two pipes pass through each other and the 'defective region' tag repeats
dimension figures are invented and garbled
uppercase regular titles are heavier than the light system
invented commitments (days, process names) read as facts
tile sizes are uneven, leaving step 02 text crammed beside the drawing
no steel-blue accent to mark focus
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone tiles, huge light numerals, light headline, mono tags, line drawing and square corners are the brand book almost verbatim.
